- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peak at 1–2% below true peak.
- If sentiment turns positive mid-horizon (e.g., +0.2+), model often underreacts — increase forecast slope slightly to match sentiment momentum.
- Model consistently overestimates 30-day mean by 2–4% when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — adjust downward by 1–2% for 15–30 day horizons.
- When sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating +/–0.3), model tends to smooth too much — allow 1–2% asymmetric jitter in forecast to reflect sentiment noise.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model often ignores sentiment decay — if sentiment drops below -0.3 after day 10, reduce forecast slope by 10–15% to reflect mean reversion.
